hero.title: SGT University
hero.summary: SGT University’s Faculty of Agricultural Sciences offers undergraduate agriculture and specialist postgraduate study near Gurugram. Its course account includes farm work, protected cultivation and rural and industry attachments. The audited ICAR entry names both undergraduate agriculture and postgraduate agronomy.

overview.heading: Agriculture with rural and industry attachments
paragraphs: SGT’s undergraduate programme description combines crop, soil and plant-health subjects with practical components. It identifies Rural Agricultural Work Experience, Agro-Industrial Attachment and experiential learning units. These named components make the practical structure clearer than a general promise of hands-on study.

The university also advertises several agricultural master’s courses. Agronomy provides one route into specialist crop-management study after an agriculture bachelor’s degree. Published eligibility figures vary between an older 2024-25 schedule and the undated current undergraduate page, so applicants should use the final intake notice to settle the marks threshold before applying.

admissions.heading: Planning an agriculture application
admissions.intro: SGT’s 2026-27 procedure describes online registration, an application form, a registration payment and an online personal interview. Admission is subject to eligibility and applicable regulatory provisions.

steps.title: Register and select the programme
steps.text: The official procedure asks applicants to choose a programme or specialisation and generate a brochure number.

steps.title: Complete the application
steps.text: The procedure specifies a registration fee of INR 1,500 and confirmation by SMS or email.

steps.title: Attend the interview
steps.text: The 2026-27 page describes an online personal interview before eligible candidates proceed to provisional admission.

documents: Common university FAQ: originals of Class 10 and 12 marksheets and pass certificates.
For PG applicants: graduation marksheets and degree.
Photographs of the applicant and parents, Aadhaar copy, and original character/migration certificates.
Haryana domicile, caste or gap certificates where applicable; confirm the checklist for your category.

campus.heading: Research farms and protected cultivation
campus.intro: The B.Sc. page describes laboratory experiments, research-farm activities and polyhouses alongside rural work and agro-industry attachment. These are programme components, not verified employment outcomes.

facilities.name: Research farm and polyhouses
facilities.description: Named in the undergraduate programme’s practical-learning account.

practical_learning: Rural Agricultural Work Experience, Agro-Industrial Attachment and experiential learning units are named in the programme description.

student_services.name: Optional campus accommodation
student_services.description: SGT describes separate hostels for boys and girls and says residence is optional. Its undated tariff lacks an explicit period, so no annual room price is inferred.

student_services.name: Day-scholar transport
student_services.description: Students apply for pickup point and route through ERP; the transport team approves the request and issues a bus pass.

student_services.name: Health and student support
student_services.description: The FAQ identifies access to SGT Hospital, counselling and mental-health support for hostel residents.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships and financial support
scholarships.text: The agriculture masters landing explicitly excludes M.Sc. Ag. Agronomy from its displayed postgraduate merit-scholarship scheme. Other listed agriculture/horticulture programmes have UG-mark-based tuition concessions on that page. B.Sc. applicants and Agronomy applicants should obtain the policy for their own programme rather than assume those awards apply.

schemes.name: Agriculture masters merit scheme: Agronomy exclusion
schemes.details: M.Sc. Ag. Agronomy is expressly excluded from the landing page’s postgraduate merit scheme. The page is undated and does not establish an award for a B.Sc. Agriculture applicant.

placements.heading: Career support and outcomes
placements.text: SGT University publishes an Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission for NIRF 2026. Its programme-duration cohorts report the graduating group, students placed, students entering higher studies and the median salary of placed graduates. These historical institutional submissions are not a placement promise or a salary estimate for every student or individual specialisation.

statistics.label: UG four-year programme category outcomes 2024-25
statistics.value: 40 graduates in minimum stipulated time; 5 placed; 30 selected for higher studies; median annual salary of placed graduates INR 2,40,000.
statistics.reporting_source: NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors; institution-submitted data, not an independently audited placement guarantee

faqs.question: Does SGT’s ICAR record include postgraduate agronomy?
faqs.answer: Yes. The audited row prints M.Sc. (Ag) Agronomy as well as B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture.

faqs.question: What practical attachments are described?
faqs.answer: The B.Sc. page names rural agricultural work, agro-industrial attachment and experiential learning units.

faqs.question: What does the 2026-27 application procedure cost?
faqs.answer: The university procedure specifies INR 1,500 for registration.

faqs.question: Is an interview described?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 2026-27 procedure describes an online personal interview before provisional admission.

faqs.question: Are the course-page fees confirmed for 2026-27?
faqs.answer: The undergraduate page gives INR 87,500 per semester without a year. This has not been treated as a dated 2026-27 quotation.
